summary: Remove the mismatching 94/326 reference, retaining 60/25.

summary: Extend the citation to cover the beginning of the quotation in verse 24.
rationale: The supplied verse 60/24 contains both occurrences of hawo k-omər “i=aṯtáyḏi-yo”; verse 60/25 begins hul d-ko-bəṭli. The example quotes both adjacent verses, so 60/25 alone omits the beginning. The additional citation 94/326 is left as supporting evidence for ko-bəṭli.

summary: Abandoning inquiry belongs to cessation I.1.
rationale: PrS 24/39 reproduces the existing passage and continues with giving up speaking of the daughter; cessation is asserted, fatigue is not.

summary: File the example about giving up the search under sense 1.

summary: New sense 3: vergeblich, zwecklos sein
rationale: 59/81 predicates futility of dealing with an opponent, rather than fatigue or ending an event. One attestation; fixed aʕm- government unproven.

data.translation: The Arab sheikh says, ‘Boy, did you get tired? Take yourself a nap for a second!’ He says, ‘No! I didn’t get tired, make me a bit of coffee, Ḥazna!’

data.translation: Ein, zwei, drei, vier Tage, da setzte sich der Teufel in das Herz ihrer Mutter, und sie sprach zu den Schwiegertöchtern: "Warum sollen wir so müßig hier im Hause bleiben? Unsere Männer gehen ins Gebirge, in die Steppe, und reiten dort herum.

summary: qaṭəl forms often express present resultant fatigue. Feminine finite baṭilo contrasts with feminine Part act. baṭəlto. PrS 15/49 female-speaker baṭilono is provisionally corrected to Preterit Intransitive, matching 113/180.
II has activity objects: rain, music, war, kroxo and a ftile. German fatigue renderings do not turn transitive II kroxo into I.2.
The unnumbered mill example and objectless PrS 57/37 leave ambiguity between II.4 and II.1 with an omitted object; the mill is not forcibly refiled.
94/519 mabəṭloniṯo expresses causative fatigue as a derived adjective, with no independently attested III finite paradigm here.
Parallel PrS references reproduce existing trade, search, courting and mill quotations; no duplicate examples added or reference concordances invented.
